newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen little changed despite surge in JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen little changed despite surge in JGBs.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract was little changed by midday on Friday despite a sharp rise in Japanese government bond futures, traders said.

"The key (September) JGB futures contract rose sharply, partly because technical charts turned positive, but December euroyen futures didn't follow suit as they are already at a relatively high level," a trader for a major brokerage house said.
The December stood at 99.06 by midday, up slightly from the previous day's settlement of 99.05.
Turnover was 23,508 contracts.
The December's heaviness on the upside was also due to large-lot sell orders, a city bank trader said.
"It's becoming easier to buy, as concern about a possible rise in interest rates in July or August has steadily receded, especially after Sakakibara's comments on Thursday," the trader said.
"But euroyen futures were heavy on top as sell orders worth about 1,000 to 2,000 contracts were seen," he said.
The December will likely move in a range of about 98.95 to 99.15 over the next week, a trader for another city bank said.

The market is now hoping that the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey due on June 25, will help dispel the possibility of an early rate interest rise in around September or October, the third trader said.
"Market players will probably begin buying euroyen futures as the tankan approaches, based on such a view, and an upside test to about 99.15 is possible," he said.

Market will be focusing on January-March gross domestic product data due at 0630 GMT, traders said. If the data shows GDP growth of less than four to five percent on annualised basis, euroyen futures may be bought, the third trader said.
The BOJ drained a net 200 billion yen from the money market on Friday, offsetting a projected fund surplus of 200 billion yen going into the day.
Friday is the last day of the current bank reserves reporting period.
The key overnight call rate was most actively traded around 0.43 percent to 0.44 percent this morning, down from Thursday's weighted average of 0.46 percent, traders said.
But the key rate may become a bit firmer, as there was some talk that a city bank still needed to pile up more reserves to meet required levels, traders said.
About 60 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) had been issued at 0.59 percent as of 0314 GMT.
About 20 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.57 percent. Two-month CDs were offered at 0.58 percent.
All CD rates were unchanged from the previous day.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, three-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.50/54 percent as of 0316 GMT, down from about 1.52/56 percent on Thursday.
The 10-year IRS rate was quoted at 2.83/87 percent, down from 2.86/90 percent on Thursday.
